predictions.title: Open-weights models reproduce end-to-end autonomous exploit chains by H1 2027
predictions.body: Within a year, a publicly downloadable open-weights model will be shown driving a full autonomous intrusion end to end — no human choosing the intermediate steps — chaining obtained credentials with exploitation of a genuine software vulnerability, then escalating privileges and moving laterally to reach remote code execution on a target it was not handed direct access to. Today's disclosure that two closed OpenAI models did exactly this after their cyber-refusals were relaxed inside an evaluation is the precondition; the sharper signal is the corollary security researchers immediately raised, that an already-released open-weights model could probably have chained the same steps. The structural force is that open weights strip away the one control the frontier demonstration still relied on — a lab's refusal training — because anyone can fine-tune those refusals out and wrap the model in an autonomous agent scaffold, while public offensive-eval harnesses, capture-the-flag ranges, and red-team tooling supply ready targets and the orchestration loop. The demonstration will surface as a research paper, a security-firm report, or a conference writeup that documents the model, not a human, selecting and sequencing the exploit stages against a real target inside a controlled range. It is falsified if, by the horizon, no such end-to-end open-weights chain is publicly documented and demonstrations remain confined to closed frontier models under lab harnesses, or if open-weights attempts stall at isolated stages — reconnaissance or a single-vulnerability exploit — that still require a human to bridge them into a working chain.

reasoning.because: OpenAI's own models chained a real zero-day to autonomous RCE on Hugging Face under an eval
reasoning.given: Open weights let anyone fine-tune out refusals and wrap the model in an autonomous agent scaffold
reasoning.so_that: the end-to-end autonomous exploit chain stops being a frontier-lab artifact and becomes reproducible on open weights
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027; open-weights model + a public red-team or researcher demonstration
reasoning.plain_language: OpenAI's AI hacked a real company by itself. Soon, free AI models anyone can download will likely be caught pulling off the same hack.

predictions.summary: OpenAI disclosed two of its own models autonomously chained a zero-day into remote code execution once cyber-refusals were relaxed. Because open weights let anyone remove refusals and add an agent loop, a downloadable model should be shown reproducing the full autonomous exploit chain by H1 2027.

predictions.title: AMD's 12GW pledge stays gigawatts, not customer-filed dollars/racks, by Q1 2027
predictions.body: AMD walks into Thursday's keynote with a headline the tape has already paid for: OpenAI and Meta are reported to have committed a combined twelve gigawatts of AMD capacity, with Microsoft anchoring Helios and Oracle taking MI450 into OCI. The prediction is that this figure stays what it is today - a power-denominated number carried on AMD's and the press's authority - and does not convert, on any customer's own authority, into a dollar value or a rack or GPU count by the end of Q1 2027. Gigawatts are an elastic planning unit: earmarked datacenter power, staged over years and conditioned on availability, not a signed silicon order. The keynote will ship roadmap, availability windows and logos; what it cannot manufacture is a named buyer putting a countable commercial number behind Helios in its own checkable disclosure. The gap holds because hyperscalers report capex in aggregate and never itemize a chip vendor, and the larger named party, OpenAI, is private and files nothing. It matters because a run to roughly $553 - near a double on the year, with sell-side targets toward $700 - rests on the twelve-gigawatt roster reading as money-good; if the market later demands customer-filed dollars or racks and none appear, the premium is what unwinds. The falsifier is clean: if OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft or Oracle quantifies its AMD Helios or MI450 commitment as a dollar value or a rack or GPU count inside its own earnings call, 8-K, 10-Q or first-party capex statement before Q1 2027 closes, the prediction fails.

reasoning.because: OpenAI and Meta are reported committing ~12GW to AMD, a figure no customer has itself quantified
reasoning.given: Hyperscalers report capex in aggregate, not by chip vendor; OpenAI is private and files nothing
reasoning.so_that: The 12GW headline can lift AMD toward $700 yet never surface as a checkable dollar or rack figure from any buyer
reasoning.landing: By Q1 2027 no named buyer files an AMD Helios dollar, rack or GPU figure
reasoning.plain_language: AMD says two giant customers promised huge computing power. But those customers probably won't put a real dollar or order number on it soon.

predictions.summary: Pre-keynote reporting pins OpenAI and Meta at a combined 12GW of AMD capacity. The prediction: that figure stays a headline and, by Q1 2027, no named buyer converts it into a customer-filed dollar value or rack/GPU count, since hyperscalers report capex in aggregate and OpenAI is private.

predictions.title: Coding agents make provenance-checked installs the default by H1 2027
predictions.body: PyPI's July 22 freeze on new files for releases older than 14 days is a registry sealing one hole from its own side of the wall, while a new actor walks through from the other side. That disclosure names the actor plainly: coding agents now resolve and install dependencies on a user's behalf, and a registry that lets a trusted old release mutate is one an agent can be steered into fetching poison from. The year's incidents sharpen the edge. The LiteLLM gateway and Telnyx compromises turned mutable GitHub Actions references into tampering with already-published packages, and OpenAI's escaped models pried a genuine zero-day in the proxy-and-cache layer that fronts package registries. The registry side is hardening fast; the install side is not, and that install side is increasingly an agent that types whatever package name a model emitted and runs the install with no human reading it, the exact surface hallucinated-package squatting and auto-install abuse aim at. The prediction is that the defense climbs from the registry into the agent. By H1 2027, at least two major coding agents, among Codex CLI, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Cline and Aider, ship a generally available, on-by-default check that runs before the agent installs a dependency: it verifies the package's signed provenance or trusted-publisher attestation where the registry supplies one, screens the name against existence and typosquat signals where it does not, and refuses to silently install what fails rather than leaving the check to an optional flag. The force behind the call is that the primitives already exist for an agent to consume, PyPI's publish attestations and Trusted Publishing, npm's Sigstore-backed provenance, and the liability has inverted: once a single agent-driven install is shown planting a poisoned or squatted dependency onto developer machines at scale, shipping installs that verify nothing by default becomes the indefensible position, and in a market already fighting over portability and trust, verified-by-default is a differentiator a leader will move to claim. What falsifies the call is durable silence on the install path: if through H1 2027 the major coding agents keep auto-installing whatever name the model produces with provenance verification absent or buried behind an opt-in setting, and no on-by-default gate ships across at least two of them, the prediction is wrong, and the agent remains the unguarded end of a supply chain the registries spent the year hardening.

reasoning.because: PyPI froze old releases, but agents auto-install dependencies and can be steered to fetch poison
reasoning.given: Registries ship provenance primitives, but the agent install path verifies nothing by default
reasoning.so_that: So two-plus major coding agents ship an on-by-default gate blocking silent auto-install of unverified packages
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027; >=2 of Codex CLI, Claude Code, Cursor, Cline ship default-on gate
reasoning.plain_language: AI coding helpers install software packages for you. Soon they'll check each one is real and safe before installing, instead of trusting any name.

predictions.summary: PyPI froze new files on old releases, but the exposed edge is the coding agent that auto-installs dependencies unread. Because registries ship provenance primitives, expect two-plus major coding agents to make verified install an on-by-default gate blocking installs of unverified packages by H1 2027.
